analyzed_vuln.description: Heap OOB read in VM is caused by malformed irep generated in scope_finish(): it reallocates the instruction buffer with size `sizeof(mrb_code)*s->pc + catchsize` and stores catch handlers immediately after iseq, but `irep->ilen` is set to `s->pc` (instruction count). The VM (`mrb_vm_exec`) indexes `pool[b]`/`syms[b]` based on decoded bytecode; with crafted source, codegen emits bytecode whose operand indexes exceed the actual pool/syms lengths, so VM reads past allocated arrays. Root cause is missing consistency/bounds validation of generated irep metadata/instruction operands at codegen finalization, not the VM dispatch itself.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Triggered via mruby_fuzzer loading attacker-controlled source (`mrb_load_string`). A short malformed input (e.g. `\xff=91327;9`) drives parser+codegen to produce inconsistent irep state during `scope_finish` (instruction stream/final tables not coherently validated). When `mrb_top_run` executes that irep, `mrb_vm_exec` executes OP_LOADL with out-of-range pool index and performs a 1-byte read just past a 10-byte allocation, causing ASan heap-buffer-overflow.
